quote.text: Most adults have had a number of really bad moments, and of course not even fairly happy people manage to be happy the whole darn time.
It's so hard to find the words when all you really want to say is: "I can see you're hurting."

Becasue that was a parents job: to provide shoulders. Shoulders for your children to sit on when they're little so they can see the world, then stand on when they get older so they can reach the clouds, and sometimes lean aganst whenever they stumble and feel unsure.
She hoped they were, because sometimes it's easier to live with your own anxieties if you know that no one else is happy, either.
Because the terrible thing about becoming an adult is being forced to realize that absolutely nobody care about us, we have to deal with everything ourselves now, find out how the whole world works.
Life doesn't turn out the way you expect.
Life can go all sorts of different ways, but it will probably go wrong.

Even astonishingly late in life, people seem incapable of considering that their parents might not be super-smart and really funny and immortal. Perhaps there's a biological reason for that, that up to a certain age a child loves you unconditionally and hopelessly for one single reason: you're theirs. Which is a pretty smart move on biology's part, you have to give it that.

That's the sort of thing you never really notice until you belong to someone else, the fact that those of us give children their names are the least willing to use them. We give those we love nicknames, because love requires a word that belongs to us alone.

When you are infatuated you can't think about anything else, you forget about your friends, your work, your lunch. If we were infatuated all the tiime we'd have starve to death. And being in love means being infatuated ... from time to time. You have to be sensible. The problem is that everything is relative, happiness is based on expectations, and we have the Internet now. A whole world constatly asking us: "But is your life as perfect as this? Well? How about now? Is it as perfect as this? If it isn't, change it!"
When you're a child you long to be an adult and decide everything for yourself, but when you're an adult you realize that's the worst part of it.
.. although you might be able to drum religion into people, you can't teach faith.
Addicts are addicted to their drugs, and their families are addicted to hope.

There were eternities between her and everyone else now, between her and the person she had been that morning. She wasn't alone in the apartment, but no one in the world shared her prospects, and that's the greatest lonelinesss in the world: when no one is walking beside you toward your destination.

We've created lives where we can watch other people crash into the wall but still hope that somehow we're going to pass straight through it. The closer we get, the more confidently we believe that some unlikely solution is miraculously going to save us, while everyone watching us is just waiting for the crash.
God doesn't protect people from knives, sweetheart. That's why god gave us other people, so we can protect each other.

The hardest thing about death is the grammar, the tense, the fact that she won't be angry when she sees that he's bought a new sofa without consulting her first. She won't be anything. She isn't on her way home. She was.

Most people aren't greedy, most people are just .... : they're just looking for something to cling on to. Something to fight for. They want somewhere to live, somewhere to raise their children, live their lives.

They say that a person's personality is the sum of their experiences. But this isn't true, at least not entirely, because if our past was all that defined us, we'd never be able to put up with ourselves. We need to be allowed to convince ourselves that we're more than the mistakes we made yesterday. That we are all of our next choices, too, all of our tomorrows.
If you want to make God laugh, tell him your plans.
